title: Code, figures, and data for the preprint "Smooth Surrogate Models Approve Impossible Firing Patterns: A Hidden Flaw in Writing Brain Codes" (Peilin (Larry) Zhong, 2026)
description: Code, figures, and data for the preprint. A smooth differentiable surrogate of a neuron's firing-rate (f-I) curve silently certifies target firing rates the real neuron cannot produce, while reporting zero optimization error. The failure is a signature of the target cell's onset bifurcation class, present in Type-II models (Hodgkin-Huxley, and Connor-Stevens in its Type-II configuration) and absent in Type-I models (Connor-Stevens Type-I and the Wang-Buzsaki hippocampal interneuron), and it is robust to sodium/potassium conductance variation. Version 1.2.0 added the minimal-model demonstration: in the two-variable Morris-Lecar model a single parameter switch between SNIC and Andronov-Hopf onset creates or removes the low-rate gap, showing that the gap is a property of the onset bifurcation rather than of channel complexity. Version 1.3.0 was a manuscript-only revision (scope statement on closed-loop and time-varying stimulation, plus reference and style corrections). Version 1.4.0 refines the Morris-Lecar onset sweep to a 0.5 uA/cm2 grid, which resolves the Hopf-regime floor more accurately (10.0 to 8.75 Hz, with the manuscript updated to match), and fixes the Type-I panels of figures 5 and S1, where the silent and firing branches had been drawn as separate polylines and left a one-grid-step visual gap in the panels whose point is that no gap exists. Results and conclusions are unchanged. The failure is invariant to surrogate fit quality, and a feasibility screen against the true f-I removes it.
